title: Father and Friend, Thy Light, Thy Love
description: Father and Friend, Thy Light, Thy Love in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 473 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “God's sustaining Presence”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther and friend, thy light, thy love Beam-ing through all thy works we see; Thy glo-ry gilds the heavens a-bove, And all the earth is full of thee.

lines: Father and friend, thy light, thy love
Beaming through all thy works we see;
Thy glory gilds the heavens above,
And all the earth is full of thee.
Thy voice we hear, thy presence feel,
Whilst thou, too pure for mortal sight,
Reignest the Lord of life and light.
We know not in what hallowed part
Of the wide heavens thy throne may be;
But this we know, — that where thou art,
Strength, wisdom, goodness, dwell with thee.
Thy children shall not faint nor fear,
Since thou, their God, art everywhere,
They cannot be where thou art not.

licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
